IP multicast is a method of sending Internet Protocol (IP) datagrams to a group of interested receivers in a single transmission.

IGMP snooping is used to manage IP multicast traffic on layer-2 networks. IP multicast is described in RFC 1112. IP multicast was first standardized in 1986.

In contrast, a unicast router needs to know how to reach all other unicast addresses in the Internet, even if it does this using just a default route.

One such scheme, proposed by Cisco, is PGM (originally Pretty Good Multicasting, but changed for trademark reasons to Pragmatic General Multicast), documented in RFC 3208.

The Eiffel Tower ( EYE-fəl; French: Tour Eiffel [tuʁ ɛfɛl] ) is a lattice tower on the Champ de Mars in Paris, France.

Due to the addition of a broadcasting aerial at the top of the tower in 1957, it is now taller than the Chrysler Building by 11 metres (36 ft).

The Eiffel Tower sways by up to 9 cm (3+1⁄2 in) in the wind.

It opened in 1894 and is 158.1 m (519 ft) tall. Tokyo Tower in Japan, built as a communications tower in 1958, was also inspired by the Eiffel Tower.

T4 is a relatively large virus, at approximately 90 nm wide and 200 nm long (most viruses range from 25 to 200 nm in length).

## 1. What tripped the old classifier (measured BEFORE I changed anything)
`classifyTurn` + `planTurn`, unmodified, on the 135 frozen round-1 phrasings (`g1/baseline-output.txt`), then on all 371 phrasings of five rounds (`g1/baseline-vs-new.json`):

| measure (371 phrasings, 268 ask for output, 103 do not) | old | new |
|---|---|---|

| false "generate / compose / transform / code" on non-requests | 13.6% (14/103) | 0% (0/103) |
| non-English asks (es, fr, ru, de, zh) read as output | 0% (0/29) | 100% (29/29) type-exact |

| …contains the topic and no instruction | 27.1% (23/85) | 100% (85/85) |
| anaphoric asks ("write me an essay on this") whose query carries the thread's topic | 3.8% (1/26) | 100% (26/26) |
| poems / stories / jokes / taglines / personal writing that are searched although they ground in nothing | 82.1% (138/168) | 0 (all 168 read `needsSources:false`) |

The causes, in the order they cost the most:
1. **The query is the instruction.** `planTurn` treats "write me an essay on this" as an elliptical follow-up (it has "this") and searches the first words of the ask plus the earlier ask's content words: `write essay invented telephone` (reproduced on the real page, section 5). For a plain "write an essay about dolphins" the query is the whole sentence. Nothing in the pipeline had a notion of the topic apart from the instruction.
2. **`GENERATE_RE` is a verb within 40 characters of a noun.** No word order, no language, no typos, no nominal asks ("essay on the Roman Empire", "I need an essay…", "tell me a joke", "now a poem about it"), and no way to say "this is a question ABOUT writing": it fired on "how do I write an essay", "make sure you note that…", "why did he write the letter", "is it ok to write in first person", "how to write a cover letter".
3. **Every generate turn is searched.** Poems, jokes, taglines were front-loaded with a web search and then briefed "work ONLY from the sources" (GENERATE_NUDGE). 5. **No typed void.** Nothing said "no topic", "no material", "unsupported type" before the search ran.

`describeOutput(turn, { prior, hasMaterial })` returns `{ type, form, typed, topic, topicVia, constraints, needsSources, searchQuery, material, voidIfMissing, steps, sequence, wants }`.
Types: the brief's list plus `rewrite` (a proofread / "make this shorter" has a different void from a translation or a summary). Code decides; the model is never asked unless the code is undecided (section 4).
It is gates, each with a test that fails without it (mutation check, section 3):

| gate | rule | measured example it removes |
|---|---|---|
| G1 question-frame | a wh-word, auxiliary, modal or negat… [8200 more chars at the transcript address]

text:
Done: the Stop button beside the answer is gone. The composer's send button still turns into Stop for the whole turn, and Esc still stops it. I haven't reloaded the page to check the new styling.

**Structure mocks** are in too, so all three stage designers have delivered. They're in `docs/playback/structure/`: `seg.html`, `con.html`, `syn.html`, with 72 screenshots and a README.
- **SEG:** a partition of a line. It keeps your SUBJ/VERB/OBJ grid look, but the boxes are drawn over the verbatim sentence in the page's own type. Nothing is struck through or reworded.
- **CON:** a convergence. Pages run into one shared name and fan out into what each says. Only words shared between pages are bold, and pages that never use the name get a dashed "Not joined" card.
- **SYN:** a typeset composite. The answer sentence is set from its sources, with copied runs in the source's face and a favicon, and the model's own words in italic. Each run opens a card showing its source line, so the seams are visible.

Faces switch with a three-stop dial and breadcrumbs, and tapping any atom opens the source with prev/next lines.

**Real findings from the recorded data**
- **Wrong source cited:** the Great Wall answer is verbatim on halleyspace.com, but the record cites checkthisfact.com. The cited line there reads "is visible from space.", which says the opposite.
- **Stitched answer:** the second sentence is stitched from two lines of one page.
- **Telephone sentence:** marked ungrounded even though 13 of its 24 words are copied.
- **President turn:** its pages name Donald Trump on 3 pages, while "Joe Biden" is on 2 of 5.

**Gaps in what the tape records**
- The cut isn't recorded, and neither are page offsets for kept lines.
- Cite spans carry no passage id.
- There are no `draft` entries, so SYN can't be replayed in time.
- The CON "same thing" rule only handles English capitalised names.

**Still unresolved:** the machine load is unchanged at about 150, so the timing numbers from the effort-level and speed agents are still unreliable. Tell me if you want those paused.

Still running: the two generation agents, effort levels, speed, the carry bug, the no-model ceiling, precise snips, discourse memory, and nested pop-ups.

text:
I'm not sure what set off the "wtf?". Two things on screen could plausibly have, and one is clearly wrong.

**The answer in the app is wrong.** You asked "who wrote Pride and Prejudice?". The model's sentences couldn't be traced to the pages it read, so the app fell back to the sources' own words. What it showed was a paragraph about the 2005 film (director, release dates, box office), and the author's name appears nowhere in it. The snip picker matches on the words in the question ("pride", "prejudice") and doesn't know that "who wrote" wants a person's name. That's the "more info than needed" problem you raised, in its worst form. The precise-snip agent (P2) is on exactly this, but its fix isn't in yet.

**The machine is badly overloaded.** Load average is 179 with 311 node processes, which is why web searches are failing with 502s and the agents' timings are unreliable. That's from the agents' parallel runs plus your other sessions. I can pause some agents. Tell me if you want that.

**One agent finished:** the generation-request classifier agent (G1).
- **What changed:**
  - It rewrote `classifyTurn` in `fold-chat-discourse.js`, and that change is live.
  - It added a pure `fold-chat-outputtype.js`, with 31 tests, that returns the output type, the topic resolved through the thread, and what's missing.
- **Its own numbers:**
  - The old classifier read 58.6% of writing requests as writing requests and put an instruction word in the search text 72.9% of the time. The new one reads 99.3% correctly on the agent's own corpus.
  - On rounds it hadn't designed for, exact type accuracy was about 82–95%, and the agent says its round-1 96% was overfit.
- **What's not applied:** the changes to `fold-chat.js` are an unapplied diff. Until I apply it, a request like "essay on this" still searches with the instruction word in the query. I haven't applied it, because it changes real behavior and the other generation agent (G2) is feeding off the same shape.

What did you mean by "wtf?"

result: {"stdout":"B:f6a706c353:8103 Monte Everest 77364
El monte Everest o Éverest​ es la montaña más alta de la superficie del planeta Tierra,​ con una altitud de 8848,86 metros (29 032 pies) sobre el nivel del mar.​​ Está localizada en el continente asiático, en la cordillera del Himalaya, concretamente en la subcordillera de Mahalangur Himal; marca la frontera entre China y Nepal, considerada como la frontera más alta del mundo.​ El macizo incluye los picos vecinos Lhotse, 8516 metros (27 940 pies); Nuptse, 7855 m (25 771 pies) y Changtse, 7580 m (24 869 pies).


== Toponimia ==

El Everest es conocido con varios nombres:

ཆོ་མོ་ལུང་མ། (Chomolungma, ‘madre del universo’) en el Tíbet;
珠穆朗瑪 (Zhūmùlǎngmǎ) en China;
Sagarmāthā (‘la frente del cielo’) en Nepal.​​
En un mapa de 1733 sobre Tíbet y Bután elaborado por el geógrafo y cartógrafo francés Jean Baptiste Bourguignon d'Anville se registra el nombre tibetano de la montaña: Tchomour Langmac
----
B:44732d5a7e:17202 Vitesse de la lumière 57211
La vitesse de la lumière dans le vide, habituellement notée c (pour « célérité »), est une constante physique de l'Univers qui est fondamentale dans plusieurs domaines de la physique. Elle est égale à 299 792 458 m/s.
L'étude de la lumière et de sa vitesse remonte à l'Antiquité. Des philosophes et des scientifiques, en s'appuyant sur des arguments théoriques ou des observations, affirment que sa vitesse est infinie, alors que d'autres prétendent que non. Ole Rømer démontre en 1676 qu'elle est finie. Les scientifiques s'attachent ensuite à déterminer sa valeur par divers moyens, la précision s'améliorant au fil des années. Dès la fin du XIXe siècle, il est acquis qu'elle vaut environ 300 000 km/s ; en 1975, le résultat fiable le plus précis est 299 792 458 ± 1 m/s. En 1983, un accord international redéfinit le mètre de telle sorte que la vitesse de la lumière est d'exactement 299 792 458 
----
B:63987dc4ba:8333 Скорость света 45769
Ско́рость све́та в вакууме — абсолютная величина скорости распространения электромагнитных волн, в точности равная 299 792 458 м/с (или приблизительно 3×108 м/с). В физике традиционно обозначается латинской буквой «
  
    
      
        c
      
    
    {\displaystyle c}
  
» (произносится как «цэ»), от лат. celeritas (скорость).
Скорость света в вакууме — фундаментальная постоянная, не зависящая от выбора инерциальной системы отсчёта (ИСО). Она относится к фундаментальным физическим постоянным, которые характеризуют не просто отдельные тела или поля, а свойства пространства-времени в целом. Из постулата причинности (любое событие может оказывать влияние только на события, происходящие позже него, и не может оказывать влияние на события, произошедшие раньше него) и постулата специальной теории относительности о независимости скорости света в вакууме от выбора инерциальной системы отсч
----
B:666fe137c9:15492 珠穆朗瑪峰 12968
珠穆朗玛峰（藏語：ཇོ་མོ་གླང་མ，威利转写：Jo mo glang ma，藏语拼音：Qomolangma，香港稱额菲尔士峰，台湾稱圣母峰），尼泊尔称萨加玛塔峰（尼泊爾語：सगरमाथा，羅馬化：Sagarmāthā），西方称埃佛勒斯峰（英語：Mount Everest，又譯額菲爾士峰、艾佛勒斯峰），是喜马拉雅山脉的主峰，是世界第一高峰，海拔8848.86米。
珠穆朗玛峰位于中华人民共和国（西藏自治区）与尼泊尔萨加玛塔专区的交界处的喜马拉雅山脉中段，北纬27°59′15.85″，东经86°55′39.51″，北坡在西藏定日县境内，南坡在尼泊尔索卢坤布县境内。
珠穆朗玛峰全年平均温度为-29°C，被称为「世界第三极」，另外兩極是指地球的北極和南極。近年来，由大约15000个冰川和世界上最高的若干个山峰组成喜马拉雅冰川正受到全球变暖的巨大威胁，冰川面积减少。由于印度板块和歐亞大陸板塊以每年5.08公分的速度互相挤压，致使整个喜马拉雅山脉仍在不断上升中，珠穆朗玛峰每年增高约1.27公分。珠峰地区居民稀少，中尼两国皆在此设立国家公园或自然保护区。1979年，联合国教科文组织将尼泊尔萨加玛塔国家公园列入世界自然遗产名录。1988年，中国设立珠穆朗玛峰国家级自然保护区，包括西藏自治区的定日县、聂拉木县、吉隆县、定结县，面积为3.38万平方公里。
清康熙五十六年（1717年），《皇舆全览图》称“朱母朗马阿林”，是最早的地圖標示。1856年，英屬印度測量局公布經緯度及海拔。1865年，英國皇家地理學會命名為「埃佛勒斯峰」。1952年，中國將「珠穆朗玛峰」定为正式名称。
1961年10月5日，《中华人民共和国和尼泊尔王国边界条约》约定两国边界线走向。其中，“珠穆朗瑪峰（萨加·玛塔）和洛子峰，到马卡鲁山”线北为中国领土，线南为尼泊尔领土。2019年10月13日，《中华人民共和国和尼泊尔联合声明》，“考虑到珠穆朗瑪峰是中尼两国友谊的永恒象征，双方愿推进气候变化、生态环境保护等方面合作。双方将共同宣布珠峰高程并开展科研合作。”
2020年12月8日，中国珠穆朗玛峰测量队登顶珠峰半年多时间

text:
Fixed, and confirmed on a real turn. It's a real regression, but not from my merge or the zip. It came in with the grounding-gate rewrite in commit `71e90a3` (2026-10-05).

**What happened**
- **The model was right.** It wrote "Pride and Prejudice was written by English author Jane Austen."
- **The Pivot threw it away** as `ungrounded:name` ("English"). With nothing left to speak, the app fell back to showing raw page text, and that's the film paragraph you pasted.
- **Page 1 says it.** The novel's page says "a novel by English author Jane Austen" but not the ask's own word "wrote". `attribute` in [fold-chat-ground.js](fold-chat-ground.js) checks the top 8 candidate windows across all passages and reported only the first failure. That was a name miss in an unrelated film page. The Pivot's rescue for frame words like "wrote" only runs for a `terms` failure, so it never ran.
- **Bisect:** the name check passes through `68a7000` and fails from `71e90a3`, and the committed code fails on the exact case.

**The fix**
- `attribute` now reports the failure of the passage that got furthest, meaning names and figures held and only a content term was missing.
- **What it can't change:** which sentences are accepted. A name no passage has (a fabricated "Charles Dickens") is still a hard failure, and a regression test pins both cases. 79/79 grounding, Pivot and attribution tests pass.
- **Verified live:** the real app now answers "who wrote pride and prejudice?" with the right sentence and the Wikipedia source card, with no fallback.
- **Not covered:** the project's gate-controls harness runs against an older snapshot in `eval/.app`, so it didn't exercise this change. It also shows many pre-existing false positives and negatives that aren't from this change. I'm not claiming it as a check.

**A second bug, also fixed:** the Interpretation designer reported that real tapes never carried `check` or `loop` entries. That was my merge, and this turn's tape now has 3 `check` entries and a `draft`. No `loop` appears because no REC lap was needed.

**Open wart:** the grounding coverage for this sentence still reads 0/1, because the plain check doesn't apply the rescue. The hover can still label a correct sentence as unsupported. Fixing it means changing how the record is built, which is bigger than this bug. Do you want that done?

title: /0c804cde-75c0-4276-bf91-3cc3a46d1c35/t1
text:
The navigation experiment is done. I confirmed the files are there and its 23 sitestyle tests pass. It's in `docs/playback/nav/`: four stacking models (`a-sheets.html`, `b-push.html`, `c-zoom.html`, `d-split.html`), a contact sheet of real sites, `sitestyle.mjs`, a README and 113 screenshots.

**Recommended model: sheet stack on narrow screens, side-by-side split at 900px and wider**
- **History:** one stack and one history rule. Opening a layer pushes a history entry. The phone's Back, the return pill, Escape, swipe and pinch all go back one layer, and a crumb or the Chat button jumps further. Back at the top of the stack stays in the document and doesn't leave the app.
- **Way back:** a 44px return pill sits at the same fixed spot (bottom-left) on every layer.
- **Breadcrumbs:** on a phone, the strips of the layers beneath are the breadcrumbs, and each strip wears its own site. On wide screens the chat stays live and keeps its scroll, and older layers fold into 40px spines.
- **Borrowed from the zoom model:** the layer grows out of the tapped marker, plus a "you were here" pulse on the way back. That model also has the lowest chrome, 52–82px.
- **Phone cost:** the sheet stack takes 12% of the screen at depth 1 and 24% at depth 5. The push model costs a constant 96px. The agent suggests about 4 layers as the comfortable cap, with push as the fallback if depth 5 or more is common.

**Wear-the-site**
- `sitestyle.mjs` reads a page's own CSS and outputs 12 validated tokens. It never copies site CSS, and ink is adjusted to keep 4.5:1 contrast, never paper.
- Across 986 cached pages (414 domains) it produced no invalid token sets.
- The contact sheet has 16 real sites and 3 labelled synthetic fixtures.

**The three open questions**
1. **Is the site identity actually there?** 44% of cached pages give no site-identity token from inline CSS alone. We'd need to fetch each page's first stylesheet, or extend the hand-written site table.
2. **Do layers 3–6 earn their depth?** Britannica's kept text was 2 lines. Page and passage may need to merge into one layer.
3. **Phone gestures:** these were tested with synthetic events only, not on a real phone or with a screen reader. The header drag also competes with scrolling.

Two of the four chat turns in the mocks (nosebleed, Marie Curie) are built from cached pages and labelled as not recorded turns. One stand-in, skyatnightmagazine.com, borrows bbc.com's tokens, also labelled.

Nothing is wired into the app yet. Still running: the speed and effort-level agents, G2 (the void for failed writing requests), the carry bug, the no-model ceiling, precise snips, and discourse memory.

input: {"file_path":"/Users/mlacy/Documents/3.0/the-fold/eval/ants/E2-RESULTS.md","content":"# E2 — where a turn's time goes, and how to cut it (results)

Ant E2, 2026-10-06/07. Pre-registration: `eval/ants/E2-PREREG.md` (written before any instrumented run). Harness and run output: `eval/ants/e2/`.
Unapplied diffs: `eval/ants/e2/*.diff` (ordered below). Nothing tracked was edited; no git add/commit/push.

**Read this first: every wall-clock number below was measured on a machine under heavy contention** (load average 100-400 for the whole session, other
ants running models and browsers; `gemma2:2b` ran at 6-10 tokens/s). Absolute seconds are therefore inflated by an unknown factor (I did not get an idle machine
to calibrate). What survives load: the *structure* (what is on the critical path, how many sequential model calls and round trips), the paired
before/after on the same questions, and counts (requests, calls, wins). Where a number is modelled rather than measured it says so.

## 1. The answer to "where does the time go"

26 timed real turns on the real page (+3 app-answered turns of ~0 s), local `gemma2:2b`, the live relay and live web:

* **TTFA == TTD on 29 of 29 turns.** The answer is *held* (the Pivot reads a draft; nothing is streamed) until every later step has run, so the person waits for
  the whole turn before reading one word. Half of all wall-clock (50%) is spent **after the answer already exists** — i.e. after the Pivot has produced the text
  that is finally shown: median 21.8 s of a 42.3 s turn; 18 of 26 turns waited >= 5 s for work that does not change the words (provenance pointing, REC laps).
* **The model's own write is only 27% of wall-clock** (median call 10.2 s: 5.7 s to the first token (prefill of a ~4.8k-char prompt), then ~16 tokens at 6.6 tok/s).
* **Search + reads are small:** web search median 1.8 s (p90 4.7 s, one 16.9 s), Wikipedia median 1.0 s; page reads median 0.6 s (p90 7.5 s, max 18.7 s). The slow tail
  of "Reading 3 pages… 11 s" is a few straggler reads (browser-direct fetch refused after 5-7 s; an 8 s timeout), not the typical read.
* **Encyclopedia-origin following costs and (so far) yields nothing:** 74 trails, **0** reached an original ("Followed the encyclopedia to its source"); it blocks the model's
  write for a median 1.6 s (8 of 26 turns >= 7 s; two at the 12 s box).
* **The REC loop never changed a word:** in 7 of 26 turns the first check broke a sentence and the loop went back (median 37 s before the answer appeared); it made 13 restatement
  model calls (163 s of model time) and **replaced 0 sentences**; a second lap added 0 sources in 3 of 3 two-lap turns.
* **Provenance pointing is the other half:** 56 pointer calls over 17 turns (3.3 per turn, 5.9 s each) + `findPrimary` (3 serial searches, 3 serial page reads, a model call per page)
  = median 20.6 s after the answer exists. They never change the answer text either.
* **Dead doors:** for every page the browser could not read itself, the chain asks 5 public proxies at once. Over 29 turns: allorigins answered 1 of 132, codetabs / corsproxy.io /
  cors.eu.org / thingproxy 0 of 132 each (660 requests, each telling a third party a page address, for 1 page). The fold's own relay answered 168 of 208; the browser's own read 10 of 142.
* No hidden CPU: between model/network steps the app computes in ms (1% of post-write time is neither model nor network; the UI and the Pivot are not the cost).

### Waterfall (baseline, medians in seconds; feed `at` + in-page fetch log)

| turn type | n | total | search (to first read) | reads | origin+prompt gap | model write | after the write (checks) | p90 total |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| facts | 16 | 57.0 | 2.4 | 1.6 | 3.0 | 10.2 | 31.3 | 101.7 |
| follow-ups (pronoun, thread) | 4 | 21.6 | 3.8 | 1.4 | 0.3 | 11.1 | 4.7 | 85.6 |
| writing requests | 3 | 28.6 | 2.9 | 3.4 | 0.1 | 8.1 | 0.3 | 35.3 |
| live asks (weather, news) | 2 | 30.5 | 2.1 | … [2869 more chars at the transcript address]

WHAT IT DOES
 1. Sources-only mode (fold-chat-strand.js snipsOf): ONE answerSpan pass over the passages read gives the smallest span that answers. It becomes the first snip, kind "span":
      text     = the mechanical final pass (named rules, re-derivable)         e.g. "The tower is 330 metres (1,083 ft) tall."
      verbatim = the page's own bytes the span was cut from (a substring of the page text, or of the declared FAQ item)
      context  = the sentence it sits in (ONE TAP AWAY: the view's "the sentence" button)
    Every other snip of the turn is `more: true` and drawn behind "more from this page": the group / declared block is never the default view. verifySnip checks a span snip
    (the verbatim bytes occur in the page and the shown text is those bytes or verifyRewrite re-derives it). With no span the groups are drawn as before and the strand
    carries `minimalGap` = the typed gap ("no sentence in what was read states this"); the chat passes it to renderStrand(…, { gap }).
    An encyclopedia passage (tertiary) never supplies the span (it is a pointer, never a source).
    Off switch: STRAND.minimal = false (or snipsOf(…, { limits: { ...STRAND, minimal: false } })).
 2. The strand view (fold-chat-strandview.js + 4 lines of CSS in index.html): the span large, "the sentence" as a toggle, "more from this page" as <details>; the typed gap line when there is no span.
 3. The slot pipeline (fold-chat-answerwire.js): `minimalOfTurn(turn, question)` cuts the smallest span from the answer's own `row.sentence` (no outside sentence, so no pronoun is
    resolved from beyond it) and `runSlotTurn` attaches it as `turn.minimal`; `answerLine(turn)` returns it. contentAllowed (answerTurnBacksContent) accepts the content being either
    the realised line or that span (the every-word-occurs-in-row.sentence check still applies). The answer CARD (fold-chat-presentview.js) should draw `turn.minimal.text` first and
    `turn.minimal.sentence` behind the same "the sentence" tap; that file is not touched here.

EOF

text:
The carry bug is fixed in the modules, but it isn't live yet: two diffs still have to be applied, and I'm holding them for a reason. The test suite is at 1896 of 1897. The one failure is the old-port check, which is `voice/thinkers-profile.json` from your other session's work, not this.

**Causes, per symptom in your stored chat**
- **"why is the sky blue" searching with McKinley carried over:** the English carry list in `fold-chat-hints.js` included "the", "one" and "there". The question passed the pronoun gate, so the previous turn's referents were prepended to the search.
- **The song bleeding into the next answer:** `modelHistory` dropped the empty assistant turn but kept your "write me a song" ask. Short chats ride along verbatim, so the model kept writing lyrics.
- **Junk referents:** a line break didn't count as a sentence start, and creative answers fed the referent list. "The", "With" and "Across" became referents.
- **Reuse of the previous turn's passages:** the merged feature that reuses them fired on standalone asks like "so what is dna" and "are you sure about gravity". That one is fixed in `fold-chat-flow.js`. It wasn't the cause of the sky-blue case.

**Fix and numbers**
- **The gate:** a new pure `fold-chat-anaphora.js` carries only pronoun or elliptical asks. It's wired through the thread, mind, flow and salience modules.
- **Style carry:** a new `fold-chat-histkind.js`, which is not wired yet.
- **Corpora:** 113 dev sequences plus 56 held-out ones frozen before any run. The gate was tuned on the dev set.

| Class | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Standalone asks wrongly inheriting | 22 of 73 | 0 of 73 |
| True follow-ups carried | 40 of 67 | 62 of 67 |
| Hard / ambiguous | 13 of 29 | 23 of 29 |

- **es/fr follow-ups:** 0 of 11 before, 9 of 11 after.
- **Real page, on a replay of your stored chat:**
  - **Search:** "why is the sky blue" now searches as just that and reads the sky-blue pages.
  - **Song question:** the draft that was a trampoline song 2 of 2 times before is now a plain answer 2 of 2 times after. In those runs the page's own checker then withheld the draft as unsupported.
  - **Caveat:** search relays were 502ing all session, so it used a Wikipedia stand-in for search. These are single samples.

**Not applied yet:** `eval/ants/g3/wire.diff` (style carry, the creative flag, and an optional hunk giving a standalone factual ask no history) and `channels.diff`. Two more diffs touch the same files: G1's `wire.diff` against `fold-chat.js` is waiting, and G2, still running, owns `channels.js`. I'd rather apply all three in one careful pass once G2 finishes, so they don't fight each other. If you'd rather I apply G3's now and reconcile later, say so.

**Left unsolved, per the agent:** es/fr clitic and pro-drop follow-ups, and "when did that happen". They fail toward no carry.

## 1. What the failure was (reproduced on the real page, not inferred)
Real page (:8815), real gemma2:2b, real search, the model transport aborted on turn 2 only (Playwright `page.route`), after "who invented the telephone?":
- **The query is the instruction.** `planTurn` searched `write essay invented telephone` (or `Alexander Graham Bell Elisha Gray write me an essay on this`, `write essay …` varies with the referent store). What came back: bartleby, gradesfixer, quora, cram, leverageedu, essays.io, papersowl, ivypanda. Not one is about the telephone as a topic; they are about writing about it.
- **The strand fallback fires for ANY kind.** `catch (modelErr)` (fold-chat.js ~2243) calls `snipsOf(webPassages)` and draws "model declined · The model could not answer (network error). Showing what the sources say instead. FROM THE SOURCES, UNCHANGED · NO MODEL WROTE THIS". Observed content of that strand: a Bartleby student essay, a gradesfixer sample, **a bot-check page** ("This website uses a security service to protect against malicious bots"), and — once the relay's recorded results were used — the leverageedu tutorial sentence "To write an essay on telephone in simple words, first start with an introduction…" — the user's screenshot, reproduced.

plus=[l[1:] for l in rej if l.startswith("+") and not l.startswith("+++") and not (l[1:].startswith("//") or l[1:].startswith("import { genVoid"))]
assert len(minus)==2 and len(plus)==2, (len(minus),len(plus))

    # the rejected hunk's lines may have been trimmed at a different width; match by exact text

input: {"file_path":"/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-mlacy-Documents-3-0-the-fold/0c804cde-75c0-4276-bf91-3cc3a46d1c35/scratchpad/results-head.md","content":"# D1 RESULTS — falsifying long-term discourse awareness (2026-10-07)

Pre-registration: `eval/ants/D1-PREREG.md` (written before any battery run; one exploratory `searchWeb` call is disclosed there). Harness: `eval/ants/d1/` (node; resumable; `out/` is git-ignored).
Nothing in the app was edited. Fixes appear only as unapplied diffs in `eval/ants/d1/proposed/`.

## What was run

| piece | what | where |
|---|---|---|
| Battery | 18 scripted conversations (12 en, 3 es, 3 fr; 30-60 turns), 118 probes at fixed distances, real Wikipedia pages recorded once and replayed byte-for-byte | `cases.json` (sha256 in the table below), `corpus/store.json`, `out/conv-*.json` |
| Sim | the live turn decision + bookkeeping of `fold-chat.js run()` over the app's OWN pure modules (planTurn, recallOf, watch, thread, salientSentences, buildTurnMessages, claimsOfTurn, applyExchange/applyCarry, freshnessOf, searchWeb over replayed fetch). The model is an extractive stand-in; everything the app decides and everything it hands the model is the app's code | `sim.mjs`, `run.mjs` |
| Clean runs | the same 45/60-turn scripts with every probe replaced by an ordinary ask, so nothing re-mentions the anchor: the forgetting curve | `out/clean-*.json` |
| Real page | `chat-live.mjs` openChat/say, gemma2:2b, real web: R1 (13 turns), R2 (7 turns), R3 (30 turns) | `real.mjs`, `out/real-R*.json` |
| Staleness, 3 sessions, ceiling | synthetic one-figure page edit; three separate chats; cold needle ceiling | `stale.mjs`, `sessions3.mjs`, `ceiling.mjs` |

Limits, stated once: (a) the `web` scope (`holodeck-proxy`) answers 502 from node, so the battery reads Wikipedia only; (b) the model in the battery is a stand-in (the real-page runs use gemma2:2b and are the check on that); (c) cells are small (118 probes over about 40 cells): read the counts, not only the percentages; (d) the Wikipedia API rate-limited the whole study (the swarm shares one IP), which set how many conversations fit.

## Live versus built-but-off (default build, read from `fold-chat.js` imports and defaults)

| mechanism | state in the default build | what it does for memory |
|---|---|---|
| turn plan: meta / elliptical / carried / push-back / source-ask (`fold-chat-thread.js`, `-flow.js`) | LIVE | reads the ask against the LAST answer only |
| referent record + carry (`fold-chat-mind.js`, `-carry.js`) | LIVE | pronouns resolve to the top-2 referents by weight; weight x0.8 per turn; cap 24 |
| thread reply (`threadTurn`) | LIVE | answers from the last answer and the passages it stored; nothing older |
| watcher PRE/POST + baton (`fold-chat-watch.js`) | LIVE | about the WORK (what was searched/read), not about facts |

All three agents' fixes (writing requests, failed-writing voids, cross-message carry) are applied and checked on the real page. Tests are 1916 of 1917; the one failure is `voice/thinkers-profile.json`, your other session's file that names the retired port.

**Applying them took more than `git apply`.** My edits to `fold-chat.js` had shifted the context, so G2's diff had 2 of 15 hunks fail and G3's had 2 of 7. I merged those by hand from the reject files. Along the way:
- **Missing import:** my first merge dropped G2's import. The live page caught it immediately ("The turn failed: KNOWN_FORMS is not defined"), and I fixed it.
- **Wiring test:** one wiring test pinned the exact `modelBarred` string. I loosened it to allow G2's one extra clause. The check itself is unchanged, since `plan || strand || aloneBarred` still bars the model.

**What I ran on the live page** (your failure sequence, gemma2:2b):

| Turn | Before | Now |
|---|---|---|
| "write me a song about trampolines" | empty answer | a real song, no web search |
| "who is mt. mckinlet named afer?" | answered as a song | not a song; an honest typed gap |
| "why is the sky blue" | searched with McKinley carried over | searched as exactly that |
| "write me an essay on this" (empty chat) | searched for essay tutorials | "can't write the essay: the request names no topic", with options, no search |

**Not confirmed:**
- The web-search relay is still returning 502, so turn 2 hit an honest gap, not an answer. I couldn't re-run your original "essay on this" after the telephone question with real pages. That's the exact case in your screenshot, and G1 and G2 tested it only with recorded pages.
- The session-wide issues are unchanged: heavy load and the other agents' runs.

**G2's policy choices that are now live, in case you disagree:**
- Sample-essay pages are set aside as material.
- A writing turn with nothing to write from draws a "can't write it" void.
- The offer button switches to Sources-only.

**Still running:** effort levels, speed, the no-model ceiling, precise snips, and discourse memory. Their reports will come as they finish.

input: {"file_path":"/Users/mlacy/Documents/3.0/the-fold/eval/ants/P1-RESULTS.md","content":"# P1 results: how complex a reasoning does the model-free machinery reach, and where is a model needed?

Ant P1, 2026-10-07. Pre-registration: `eval/ants/P1-PREREG.md` (written before any scored run; four dated amendments, all before the run they affect). Harness: `eval/ants/p1/` (node, resumable, `results/` is git-ignored run output). Every number below is produced by `p1/make-tables.mjs`, `esc-table.mjs`, `gate-eval.mjs`, `cues.mjs`, `report12.mjs`; the raw tables are in `p1/results/tables.md` (with 95% bootstrap CIs per cell).

## 0. Answer in five lines

1. **The shipped model-free machinery does not reach R2.** On 138 real-page questions, the strand (`snipsOf`), the slot pipeline, the fold/narrow pass and the khora door each fall under 70% by R2 (a figure with a unit) or R1 (slot pipeline, door). The first break is not reasoning: it is **picking the right sentence of the right page** (55-100% of the failures of the snippet arms are "page quoted, the needed fact is not in the snip").
2. **A hand-built typed-skill layer (D+, my glue, not product code) goes further**: 73% R2, 100% R6, 78% R8, 100% R9 on the battery, in 0-1 ms. But it is **template-shaped**: 12/16 on a hold-out with new entities, **1/14 on paraphrases** of questions it answered. It is an upper bound for "a figure/date binder + evaluator", not a deployable reasoner.
3. **No model-free arm tells an answerable question from an unanswerable one** (abstention discrimination: 0 to 33 points; the 2B model with a one-line instruction: 83 points). R14/R15 are "100% correct" for D+, B and E only because they abstain on everything.
4. **gemma2:2b is the wrong fix for the composition rungs and the right one for abstention, definitions and why/how.** Even with the evidence handed over (Fo) it scores R2 55%, R6 56%, R8 33%; with the product's strand (F) it scores 67/120 answerable, because the strand lacked the evidence in 29 more cases (Fo 96/120).
5. **Recommended pass-2 gate (section 5):** trust a typed skill only when it fires with evidence, route opinion/advice to a typed gap, send everything else to the model, then the pivot. On held-out questions: 77-81% correct vs 62-66% for the model alone, trust precision 0.92-1.00, every question that needed a model was escalated (recall 1.00). The pivot final pass catches inventions, not wrong reasoning (section 5.3).

## 1. What ran

138 questions, 15 rungs (8-11 each), over 51 real Wikipedia extracts from `eval/snips/cache`; each question gets its gold page(s) plus 2 distractors (R12/R13: gold only). Ground truth is code (regex / set / number / order), validated against the page bytes before any run (`node battery.mjs`).

| arm | machinery | answer text |
|---|---|---|
| A | `snipsOf`, Wikipedia URLs (the encyclopedia-lead path) | verbatim snips |
| A2 | same pages under a neutral host, so `snipsOf` takes its generic sentence path | verbatim snips |
| S | `fold-chat-salience.js salientSources` (the product's "only what is salient" selector) | verbatim excerpts |
| B | the slot pipeline (`runAnswerTurn` via `slotDeps`; Wikipedia through a cached, rate-limited fetch) | `answer.text`; handoff/gap/contest = typed gap |
| C | A + my mechanical narrow pass (idf-weighted sentence ranking, tau_c 0.5, He/She -> entity rewrite) | 1-2 whole sentences |
| D+ | `mech.mjs`: figure / date / lifespan / list-complement binder + `convertUnits` (D0 = `evaluate()` as written: **0 of 138** parse) | a templated sentence of page figures |
| E | khora read door (EORead@1) bound to the question's relation + janus `/v1/reason` over claims | the bound participant |
| F | gemma2:2b (temp 0) handed arm A2's strand | model text |
| Fg, Fo | same model, gold-ish context (Fg), ORACLE evidence sentences (Fo, diagnostic: uses my gold labels) | model text |
| G | the Pevear-Volokhonsky composite: cue-route -> D+ -> B -> E -> snippet route ->… [23985 more chars at the transcript address]

Made against the working tree as it was on 2026-10-07 (apply with `patch -p1 --dry-run < eval/ants/p2/wire.diff` first; the hunks are small and anchored on unchanged lines).

WHAT IT DOES
 1. Sources-only mode (fold-chat-strand.js snipsOf): ONE answerSpan pass over the passages read gives the smallest span that answers. It becomes the first snip, kind "span":
      text     = the mechanical final pass (named rules, re-derivable)         e.g. "The tower is 330 metres (1,083 ft) tall."
      verbatim = the page's own bytes the span was cut from (a substring of the page text, or of the declared FAQ item)
      context  = the sentence it sits in (ONE TAP AWAY: the view's "the sentence" button)
    Every other snip of the turn is `more: true` and drawn behind "more from this page": the group / declared block is never the default view. The span is NOT trusted alone: below
    confidence 0.9 (and with no second page agreeing, span.agreement) the view opens it WITH its sentence showing — measured: confidence separates right from wrong spans only weakly (AUC ~0.75). ver
    (the verbatim bytes occur in the page and the shown text is those bytes or verifyRewrite re-derives it). With no span the groups are drawn as before and the strand
    carries `minimalGap` = the typed gap ("no sentence in what was read states this"); the chat passes it to renderStrand(…, { gap }).
    An encyclopedia passage (tertiary) never supplies the span (it is a pointer, never a source).
    Off switch: STRAND.minimal = false (or snipsOf(…, { limits: { ...STRAND, minimal: false } })).
 2. The strand view (fold-chat-strandview.js + 4 lines of CSS in index.html): the span large, "the sentence" as a toggle, "more from this page" as <details>; the typed gap line when there is no span.
 3. The slot pipeline (fold-chat-answerwire.js): `minimalOfTurn(turn, question)` cuts the smallest span from the answer's own `row.sentence` (no outside sentence, so no pronoun is
    resolved from beyond it) and `runSlotTurn` attaches it as `turn.minimal`; `answerLine(turn)` returns it. contentAllowed (answerTurnBacksContent) accepts the content being either
    the realised line or that span (the every-word-occurs-in-row.sentence check still applies). The answer CARD (fold-chat-presentview.js) should draw `turn.minimal.text` first and
    `turn.minimal.sentence` behind the same "the sentence" tap; that file is not touched here.
 4. NOT wired: fold-chat.js needs no change (it already calls snipsOf and strandText); the stored message keeps `snips` (span fields verbatim/rewrite/context/more are stored by storeSnip).

**Where it breaks**
- **First failure:** it picks the wrong sentence inside the right page. The plain strand missed the answer sentence on all 51 questions in one arm, and the fold arm missed 60 of 74. Sources-only returns walls of text, with a median of 1.4–1.9k characters and none of them precise.
- **Ceilings:** most arms drop under 70% at rung R2 (a figure with a unit). The slot pipeline and khora's read door with janus drop at R1.
- **Same point as your complaint:** this matches your "more info than needed". Precise snips are the missing capability, which is why P2 is on it.
- **Even a perfect page doesn't save the small model:** with the right evidence handed to it, gemma2:2b scores only R2 55%, R6 56% and R8 33%. Only the hand-built skill code (D+), which is not product code, does better on figures and comparisons.

**Your "fold the content into a summary" idea:** as a summarizer, the fold scored 0.50 key-fact coverage against 0.85 for simply taking the first three sentences. The agent says its key facts favour the lead. The Lens and Paradigm blocks couldn't be tested at all.

**The method's gate, as measured** (a pure function in `p1/g.mjs`)
- An opinion question draws a gap, with no model.
- Otherwise, if the typed-skill code can answer with evidence, that answer is trusted.
- Otherwise the model answers from the strand, and the Pivot checks it.
- **Result:** 77% correct against 62% for the model alone across all 138 (paired +15 points, CI 9 to 22), and 81% against 66% on the held-out half.
- Every question that needed a model was escalated.

**Caveats the agent itself raised**
- **Template-shaped:** the skill code answers 12/16 held-out questions but only 1/14 paraphrases, so the gain is brittle.
- **Can't tell unanswerable from answerable:** no model-free arm can, scoring 0–33 points. The "100%" on the opinion and unanswerable rungs is vacuous abstention. gemma2:2b with one instruction scores 83.
- **The Pivot's final pass catches inventions, not wrong answers:** wrong answers went from 29 to 30 across it, and it withholds bare one-word answers as "truncated".
- **Small cells:** 8–11 questions each, so confidence intervals run about ±25 points. It tested Wikipedia only, and no model larger than gemma2:2b because qwen2.5:14b isn't installed.

**Capabilities whose absence sets each ceiling, ranked in section 6:**
1. A precise, cue-aware sentence selector (P2 is building this).
2. A typed binder that checks the subject.
3. An abstention rule.
4. Cross-source figure alignment.
5. A mechanism-sentence selector.
6. Multi-hop chaining.

Still running: P2 (precise snips), effort levels, speed, and discourse memory.

## Amendment 2 (written AFTER the 312-run main battery finished; disclosed as post hoc)
What the battery found about its own instrument: the fold's open-web search goes through the Cloudflare relay (holodeck-proxy.prometheoid.workers.dev /search?scope=web). It answered for the first ~50 runs and then answered 502 for essentially every request for the next ~3 hours (0 of 26 turns had the web scope answer in 9 consecutive blocks of 26 runs; a curl at the end still got 502). Whether our own load (about 20 searches per minute) triggered an upstream throttle or the relay was simply down is not known. Consequence: in that battery (named REGIME A, file results-e1-regimeA.json, kept in full and reported) the fast level, which has ONE scope (the web), had no fallback and returned nothing in 85% of runs, while balanced/deep fell back to the Wikipedia scope. Regime A therefore measures the levels under a failed relay, not under a healthy web.
Added, REGIME B (confirmatory for H1-H9): identical design, identical questions, 2 repeats, the same 312 runs, but ONE worker (so times are uncontended and the separate serial pass of Amendment 1 is superseded; the 4-run partial serial pass taken during the outage is kept as outage-serial-partial.json and not used), and the relay's open-web SEARCH request alone is answered by this machine's own search (the fold's local search on 127.0.0.1:8790, the same code path the page uses when it has a bridge; page reads still go through the relay and Wikipedia is still queried directly). Nothing else is stubbed: real page, real model gemma2:2b, real reads. Thresholds and hypotheses are UNCHANGED from above; they were fixed before regime B was run but after regime A's numbers were seen, which is a degree of freedom the reader should know about. Hypotheses are judged on B; A is reported next to it, with the outage-driven differences named as such (H6 is about exactly this fragility and is judged on A and B separately).
EOF
nohup node eval/ants/e1/run.mjs --workers 1 --reps 2 --proxy-search --out results-e1-regimeB.json > eval/ants/e1/run-B.log 2>&1 &

Built: `fold-chat-answerspan.js` (pure, no model; `answerSpan`, `verifyRewrite`, `classifyAsk`, `quantitiesIn`, `datesIn`, `isMinimal`, `RULES`), `fold-chat-answerspan.test.mjs` (83 tests), `eval/ants/p2/*` (harness, asks, results, mutation check), UNAPPLIED `eval/ants/p2/wire.diff`. ## The one-paragraph answer

On real pages the mechanical span is **about 15-25x more precise than what the strand shows now** (median shown text 82-120 characters against 1,450-1,600; precision against the hand-written minimal clause 0.52-0.67 vs 0.024-0.035) and it returns a typed gap on 82% of unanswerable asks where the strand ships text on 100% — **but it contains the answer in only about two asks in three (pooled out-of-sample 66.7%), no better than the strand's own 70.4%**, and its confidence barely separates right from wrong (AUC 0.65-0.75). So it must not *replace* the group: span first, its sentence one tap away (open by default when confidence < 0.9), the group behind "more from this page". Span-or-strand reaches the answer in 88.9% of pooled out-of-sample asks. Two of the pre-registered thresholds were missed on the pre-registered run and I report that first.

## 1. The pre-registered run (v1 module on HELD, run once, `results-held-v1.json`)

HELD = 89 asks over real pages: 70 answerable, 16 unanswerable, 3 asks in languages with no table (the right outcome is a typed gap). Each ask is a 3-passage turn (the page that does or does not state the answer + 2 real distractor pages). Gold (`key` = the answer, `min` = the shortest verbatim clause with its subject) was written by hand from the page text; it is checked by code to be a substring of the page. Frozen by sha before the run. The strand arm is the CURRENT `snipsOf` on the same passages (everything the user would see, all passages).

| gate (PREREG) | threshold | v1 on HELD | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| T1 contains the answer | >= 0.80 | **70.0%** (49/70; Wilson 58-79) — strand 68.6% (48/70) | **MISSED** |
| T2 median precision, all answerable (a miss counts 0) | >= 0.30 and >= 3x strand | **0.520** vs strand 0.024 (21x); hits only 0.896 vs 0.034 | met |
| T3 typed gap on unanswerable | >= 0.70 | **14/16 = 87.5%** (strand shipped text on 16/16) | met |
| T4 confident-wrong (span shipped, lacks the answer) | <= 0.10 | **20.0%** (14/70) | **MISSED** |
| T5 every shipped span verbatim-verifiable; hostile rewrites rejected | 100% | 65/65 (73/73 incl. 2nd spans, independent re-check); hostile cases rejected in tests | met |
| T6 minimality (no clause removable while answer + subject stay) | >= 0.70 of hits | **57%** (28/49) | **MISSED** |
| T7 non-English contain-or-typed-gap / confident-wrong | >= 0.75 / <= 0.10 | 77% (10/13) / **23%** (3/13) | first part met, second **MISSED** |
| T8 every gate has a test that fails when it is deleted | 100% | not measured at v1; **63/63 killed on the final module** (`mutate.mjs`) | met (final module) |

Median shown text: span 82 characters, strand 1,602. Precision quartiles (10/25/50/75/90): span 0/0/0.52/0.98/0.99; strand 0/0/0.02/0.04/0.08.

The precise-snip agent (P2) finished. Its module is built and tested, but I haven't wired it in, for a reason below. 83 of 83 tests pass, and its wiring diff applies cleanly to the current tree.

**What it built:** `fold-chat-answerspan.js`, which returns the smallest span that answers, as a character range that re-derives from the page bytes, or a typed gap. It uses no model. All 73 shipped spans on the held-out run re-derived from the page.

**Results on its pre-registered held-out set** (89 asks over real pages, run once)

| | span | strand today |
|---|---|---|
| contains the answer | 70% | 69% |
| median precision | 0.52 | 0.024 |
| median characters shown | 82 | 1,602 |
| typed gap on unanswerable | 14 of 16 | strand shipped text on 16 of 16 |

- **Your ethanol example:** over a FAQ page that doesn't state it, the strand ships 4,264 characters and the span returns "no sentence in what was read states this". Over a page that does state it, the span returns "Ethanol boils at 78.37 °C."
- **Thresholds missed:** containment (70% against an 80% bar), confident-wrong (20% against 10%) and minimality (57% against 70%).
- **Later rounds:** the agent flags the later numbers as post-hoc. Pooled over 135 asks, the span alone holds the answer 66.7% of the time against 70.4% for the strand. Span-or-strand together holds it 88.9%.
- **Confidence is weak:** it separates right from wrong only weakly (AUC 0.65–0.75).

**So it can't simply replace the long snip.** It's a lot more precise, but it misses about a third of the time. The wiring therefore shows the span first, opens its sentence by default when confidence is under 0.9, and keeps the full group one tap away.

**Main failure types:** the right page but the wrong sentence (the page uses a different verb, noun or measure than the ask, and dates are weakest), plus language misdetection on short questions full of names. The pronoun, unit and attribution rewrite rules never fired on 159 real spans, so they're tested on synthetic text only. Only en, es, fr, ru and zh have tables.

**Why I haven't applied it:** the diff touches `fold-chat-strand.js` (which has your uncommitted changes), the strand view, the slot pipeline and `index.html`, and it changes what Sources-only shows by default. I also can't confirm it on live pages while the search relay is down. If you want it, I'd apply it, run the suite, and check it on a cached-page turn. Do you want that?

Still running: effort levels, speed, and discourse memory.

p="eval/ants/E2-RESULTS.md"
s=open(p).read()
old=s[s.index("All diffs are against the working tree as of this run"):s.index("Tests that ship with the proposal")]
new='''All diffs are `patch -p1` diffs against the working tree as it stood when I generated them (fold-chat.js is being edited by other sessions; `patched/fold-chat-g.js` in the matrix was built from an earlier state of it, same edits). Within one file apply in numeric order — **page** (`fold-chat.js`): 1, 2, 6, 7 (7 needs 1 and 2); **primary**: 3; **web** (`fold-chat-web.js`): 4, 5, 8, 9 (incremental, each on the previous). I checked that all nine apply in sequence and that the result of 4+5+8+9 is byte-identical to the web file windows 3 and 4 ran. Each is behind a localStorage flag so it can be A/B'd in place; `eval/ants/e2/matrix.mjs` + `configs.mjs` is the live before/after.

By saving / risk:
1. `1-answer-first.diff` — biggest win, lowest product risk (provenance is the same code, same checks, run after the Pivot's text is on the page). 2.6x alone.
2. `2-rec-futile-lap.diff` — 11 lines, text unchanged by construction.
3. `6-origin-box.diff` — 74 trails, 0 originals; saves 4-7 s of the pre-write span.
4. `3-primary-parallel.diff` (+ `primary-par.test.mjs`) — pure waiting; same verdicts. Shrinks the background checks (all-checks-done 80.7 -> 53.4 s in window 2) so the next turn waits less.
5. `7-rec-laps-after-answer.diff` — **product decision**: laps stop restating. Largest tail cut (the 7 of 26 turns that took 25-88 s).
6. `5-read-grace.diff`, `4-direct-read-cap.diff` — small, tail-only, unit-tested (4 first in the chain).
7. `9-dead-door-memory.diff` — waste and third-party exposure, not latency.
8. `8-web-budget-grace.diff` — 3-4 s on slow-relay days, the only lever that can change which pages are read.

'''
s=s.replace(old,new)
open(p,"w").write(s)
PYEOF
grep -n "numeric order" eval/ants/E2-RESULTS.md | head -2"}

text:
input: {"message":"E2 done. Tracked files untouched, no git commands. Nine unapplied diffs, the harness, a pre-registration and the results write-up are all in place.

**Where the time goes.** I instrumented 29 real baseline turns on the real page (26 timed, 3 app-answered), with local gemma2:2b, the live relay and live web.
- The median turn took 42.3 s (facts 57.0 s, p90 101.7 s, max 113 s). Time to first answer equalled time to done on 29 of 29 turns, because the answer is held until every check has run.
- 50% of wall-clock comes after the model has finished writing. The model write itself is only 27% (median 10.2 s).
- Search is 2.9 s, reads 1.8 s. The "Reading 3 pages… 11 s" stall comes from a few straggler reads.
- The REC loop went back on 7 of 26 turns (median 37 s, up to 88 s). Its 13 restatement calls replaced 0 sentences.
- Provenance pointing adds a median of 20.6 s on the 17 turns that have it.
- Following the encyclopedia to its source succeeded on 0 of 74 trails, yet it held the write for a median of 1.6 s, and the 5–7 s gaps seen in later runs.
- Of 660 requests to five public proxies, 1 succeeded.

**Before/after.** On the same 16 ground-truth questions, run paired and interleaved, with 9 diffs applied (flags turn each off):

| | tracked code | all diffs applied |
|---|---|---|
| median time to a readable answer | 60.0 s | 12.2 s |
| p90 | 88.5 s | 42.1 s |
| paired questions faster | n/a | 14 of 16 |
| ground-truth correct | 15/16 | 14/16 |

- Answer-first alone takes the median from 81.9 s to 32.0 s.

Amendment 2b (before regime B was run): the local search on 127.0.0.1:8790 turned out to be throttled as well (Brave answered 429 to Node's fetch, then 'cooling down', for over an hour), while curl from the same address with the same User-Agent got Brave results pages. So regime B's open-web search is: heimdall's own Brave request and parser (heimdall/src/websearch.js parseBrave) fetched with curl, one live search per DISTINCT query at >= 7 s spacing, CACHED for the whole battery (every question's natural query is pre-warmed before any timed run). Consequence, declared: within regime B the three levels and both repeats of a question see the SAME search-result page, so the search engine's own run-to-run variance is removed from the noise term (page reads and the model still vary). This isolates what the levels do from what the engine does. Queries the page issues that are not the question text (reframe re-searches) are fetched live, spaced, and also cached.
EOF
nohup node eval/ants/e1/run.mjs --workers 1 --reps 2 --proxy-search --out results-e1-regimeB.json > eval/ants/e1/run-B.log 2>&1 &
sleep 240; tail -5 eval/ants/e1/run-B.log","timeout":300000}

## Amendments to the pre-registration (all written after the runs they concern; none edits a case)

1. Battery B was added after A's first analysis because A's cells were thin (about 10 probes per kind). A and B are reported pooled; the A-only numbers are in `out/summary2-A.json` and agree in direction with the pooled ones.
2. Mid-study I found that the working tree had gained a gate (G3) between my first prompt reading and my runs: an ask that does not lean on the earlier turn is handed no history and no summary. I added it to the sim as the `live` arm and kept the pre-G3 composition as the `livePreG3` arm. The real-page runs R1/R2 (00:50-01:07) ran before that edit (`fold-chat.js` 01:46); R3-R5 after.
3. The needle gold is retrieval-level ("read": the verbatim sentence is in a passage the turn read) as well as the strict model-level ("handed": it survives the app's own 4-sentences-per-page compression into the model's source block). Both are reported. This was added after I found, with the app's own `salientSentences`, that the model-facing block omits the answer sentence in 14 of 30 cold asks (`ceiling.mjs`).
4. The sim's `web` scope is dead (502) and the stand-in model always writes traceable sentences; the sim therefore under-counts searches (2-3 per ask vs 5-8 on the real page, `fidelity.mjs`) and over-fills the claim store (real gemma2:2b left the store empty on 9 of 30 R3 turns). What I ran:
- **Simulation:** it calls the app's own pure modules over replayed real Wikipedia pages. 48 conversations, 1992 turns, 316 probes (en/es/fr).
- **Model:** the simulation uses a stand-in model, so it under-counts searches.
- **Real page:** R1–R5 on gemma2:2b, 30 turns at most. The simulation agrees with the real page on 10 of 10 R2/R5 turns.

Pre-registered claims: 3 held (bounded prompt, page memo within 10 minutes, the recall pattern costing 0 searches). 17 were refuted.

1. **Grounding:** an ask after a detour names the anchor topic in 5 of 20 cases. Nearly every pronoun query (37 of 38) also carries an unrelated second referent.
2. **"What did you tell me about X":** it returned the wrong turn 7 of 8 times when a sibling topic shared a word (Great Wall vs Berlin Wall).

4. **Cost per ask:** on the real page an ask costs 5.2 searches and 8.7 page reads.

9. **Storage:** 52–80 KB per turn on the real page, reaching the 5 MB quota near turn 96; `save()` fails silently there.
10. **Stale facts:** recall served an edited-away figure silently 4 of 4 times, and corrections were searched 27 of 27 times.
11. **Cold ceiling:** the app's own 4-sentence compression drops the answer sentence in 14 of 30 cold asks.

`D1-RESULTS.md` also holds the live-vs-off map, the prompt-size and recall curves against both baselines, exact reproductions, and a ranked list of failures by how often a real user would hit them. The mark medium has a `found` and `done` entry.

Two unapplied diffs are in `eval/ants/d1/proposed/`:
- **`recall-score-and-asks.diff`:** it fixes two of the three live recall failures on a synthetic store shaped like the real runs.
- **`store-shadow-and-full-span.diff`:** it applies cleanly in a dry run.

I added a second 30-conversation battery after the first analysis, to raise n; the amendments are in the results file."}

text:
The discourse-memory agent (D1) finished, and most of what you hoped the memory did is refuted. Of 20 pre-registered claims, 3 held and 17 were refuted. The report is `eval/ants/D1-RESULTS.md`. It ran 48 conversations (1,992 turns, 316 probes in en/es/fr) by calling the app's own modules over replayed real Wikipedia pages. A second battery was added after the first analysis, with the amendments logged. It also checked 30 turns on the real page, where the real page agreed with the simulation on 10 of 10 turns.

**What held:** the prompt stays bounded (about 4K characters at turn 60), the page memo works within 10 minutes, and the recall pattern costs 0 searches.

**What broke, against your four claims**
- **Hunting for content we already have:** all 67 re-asks searched the web again. Warm sessions found the needed content 59 of 141 times and cold sessions 58 of 141, so the discourse memory added almost nothing. On the real page an ask costs 5.2 searches and 8.7 page reads, and 147 of 184 chit-chat turns ("ok", "nice") triggered a search.
- **Proper grounding for later messages:** after a detour, the ask names the anchor topic in only 5 of 20 cases. Almost every pronoun query (37 of 38) also carries an unrelated second referent. "What did you tell me about X" returned the wrong turn 7 of 8 times when a sibling topic shared a word (Great Wall vs Berlin Wall).
- **Impressions to find the way back:** at 10 turns or more, recall without a new search is 0%, against 92% for the full transcript plus stored pages. Partial cues recalled 0 of 27. A stored address resolves to bytes 88.9% of the time, so 11% are lost.
- **Forgetting usefully:**
  - The app's own 4-sentence compression drops the answer sentence in 14 of 30 cold asks.
  - Recall served a figure that had since been edited away 4 of 4 times, silently, and corrections were searched 27 of 27 times.
  - Freshness reports pages as shifted, moved or gone on 37% of comparable claims even when the pages haven't changed.

**A storage time bomb:** each turn stores 52–80 KB on the real page, so the 5 MB browser quota is reached near turn 96. `save()` fails silently there.

**Where this leaves the earlier work:** the carry-bug gate I applied (G3) is part of the fix for the prompt-history part. D1 confirms it on the real page.

**Not applied:** two diffs in `eval/ants/d1/proposed/`. One fixes two of the three live recall failures, on a synthetic store shaped like the real runs. The other applies cleanly in a dry run. Both are untouched.

**Housekeeping:** the agent's 30 MB recorded replay corpus (`eval/ants/d1/corpus/store.json`) is now git-ignored. It can be regenerated with its harness if you'd rather track it.

**Caveats:** the simulation uses a stand-in model, so it under-counts searches. The web scope returned 502s, so retrieval was Wikipedia only.

I'd start with the silent quota failure, then recall with no new search, since those are the two a real user hits soonest. Which do you want first?
